title: Text Justification (SWE Supplement)
prompt:
Implement `fullJustify(words, maxWidth)`. Pack words greedily into lines: add the next word whenever it fits with at least one space between adjacent words. Every returned line must contain exactly `maxWidth` characters.

For each line except the last, distribute the spaces as evenly as possible among the gaps. If they cannot be divided equally, the leftmost gaps receive one extra space. A nonfinal line containing one word is padded with spaces on the right. Left-justify the last line with one space between words and pad it on the right.

`words` is a list of nonempty words, each no longer than `maxWidth`; `maxWidth` is positive. Return an empty list when `words` is empty.

example.reasoning: The first line has eight spaces split evenly across two gaps. The final single-word line is padded on the right.

references.label: Original Moveworks interview report — LeetCode 68 text justification

background_note: The 2023 report identifies LeetCode 68 and describes greedy line packing and spacing. Its title says MLE, while its structured role field says SWE, so the role is unresolved; this is a general Coding supplement rather than a confirmed MLE exercise. The empty-list behavior is a practice convention.
